claims.content: The Customer wants to monitor the status of current and past auctions.
Customer
The auction-status-monitoring pages required by this use case are implemented and available in the system as Phase 1 must-have requirements.
The monitoring page uses the global site header and footer.
The monitoring page does not include Endeca navigation.
The 'JTV Current Date/Time' displayed on the monitoring page is dynamic and updates without requiring a user refresh.
The user interface contains no non-functional links or commands.
Closed auctions have been removed from the site's category pages immediately after closing (or within the configured removal interval set by the Auctioneer).
Closed auction items appear on the 'Recently-ended' page for exactly 24 hours after closing.

The Customer's account is not in 'Review Status' (locked due to unresolved auction winnings more than 7 days old); a Customer in Review Status cannot bid or monitor active auctions until a Customer Service Rep removes the restriction.
The system maintains a watch list for the Customer containing items the Customer is interested in but not bidding on.
The system maintains the Customer's bid history, including both items won and items not won from previous bids.

The system has a supporting/underlying database that is operational and populated with auction data (closing dates, bid amounts, costs, and bidder counts) from which current and past auction status can be displayed.

The Customer must have an authenticated session (be signed in) to access account-specific auction monitoring pages and the account area; if not signed in, the system redirects the Customer to the sign-in page before allowing access to monitoring views.

All supported customer-facing auction-monitoring entry points are implemented and available before the use case begins: the vanity URLs for My Current Bids (www.jtvauctions.com/mybids) and My Watch List (www.jtvauctions.com/mywatchlist), the Site Map page links, the canned-search/sidebar links (Closing Soon, Hot Items, Recently Ended, Newly Listed Items, Lowest Bid, Upcoming Items), home page top-level category navigation, and the Today's Top Auctions product modules.

The use case is triggered when the Customer accesses an auction-status monitoring page—'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History', or 'Recently Ended Auctions'—from the account area; clicks the 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', or 'My Account' link in the global site header; accesses the vanity URL www.jtvauctions.com/mybids or www.jtvauctions.com/mywatchlist; navigates to the Site Map page; clicks a canned-search/sidebar link such as 'Closing Soon', 'Hot Items', 'Recently Ended', 'Newly Listed Items', 'Lowest Bid', or 'Upcoming Items'; chooses a top-level category (jewelry, gemstones, jeweler supplies, watches, collectibles) from the home page; or clicks a product module in 'Today's Top Auctions' (outside the QuickBid button) to view that item's auction status.

The Customer initiates auction monitoring through any supported entry point: clicking the 'My Account' link in the global site header or footer to reach the 'My Account Page' hub; accessing one of the monitoring pages directly ('My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History', or 'Recently Ended Auctions') via header/footer links, account-area links, vanity URLs, or the Site Map; or selecting a category, canned-search/sidebar link, or product module. The system responds by displaying the page for the chosen entry point—the My Account hub, the selected monitoring page, or the corresponding listing/Product Details page. If the chosen canned-search/sidebar link is 'Lowest Bid', the system displays all available items sorted by current bid from lowest to highest; if it is 'Upcoming Items', the system displays a list/page of scheduled but not yet available items.

The system displays the 'My Account Page', from which the Customer can directly access four distinct monitoring views: 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History', and 'Recently Ended Auctions'.
The Customer accesses the 'My Current Bids' page from the account area or by clicking the 'My Current Bids' link in the global site header or footer.

The system displays the 'My Current Bids' page, listing the items the Customer is currently bidding on. The list is sorted by ending time (soonest on top) by default, and the system displays a dynamic current date/time that updates without requiring a user refresh.
The Customer can sort the bid list by clicking on the column headers to reorder the data.

If the Customer's current bid for an item is less than the Current High Bid, the system displays the dollar amount in the 'My Current Bid' column in bold red text, visually indicating an outbid status.
The Customer clicks the Item # link (or the 'Bid' button) to navigate to the Product Details (Bidding) page for a specific item.

The system displays the Product Details page for the selected item, which includes real-time auction status metrics: 'Current High Bid', 'Opening Bid', 'Bid Increment', 'QuickBid Amount', open/close date/time, and a dynamic 'Time Remaining' countdown.

The system presents an 'Item Bid History' table on the Product Details page, listing bidder names, bid amounts, date/time placed, and whether each bid was a SmartBid; the most recent bids appear on top, up to 25 bids.
The Customer accesses the 'My Watch List' page from the account area or by clicking the 'My Watch List' link in the global site header or footer.
The system displays the 'My Watch List' page, listing the items the Customer is interested in but not currently bidding on, sorted by ending time (soonest on top) by default.
The Customer accesses the 'My Bid History' page from the account area or via the 'My Bid History' link in the global footer.
The system displays the 'My Bid History' page, divided into two sections—'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win'—sorted by ending time with the most recent auctions on top.
In the 'Items I've Won' section, the system displays a 'Payment Status' column; if the item has not been paid, the text appears in bold red and links to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page.

The Customer accesses the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page from the account area or by clicking the 'Recently Ended Auctions' link available on the 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', or 'My Bid History' pages.

The system displays the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page, showing closed auctions that have been removed from category pages. The table lists Item #, Description, Auction Number, Winning Amount, Winner, and Ending Time, sorted by closing time with the most recent at the top; items appear for 24 hours after closing.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of presenting the four normal monitoring views from the My Account Page, if the Customer's default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments and there are unpaid auction winnings, the system displays a 'Winning Alert' sidewise text bar notifying the Customer of the unpaid winnings and providing a link to the 'Returning Winners Payments' page, diverting the Customer from the standard monitoring navigation.

Diverges from Step 2: While the My Account Page is displayed, if the Customer has won an auction, the system displays a red 'Winner Alert!' banner in the global header with the message 'You're a Winner!' and a clickable 'Click Here Now' link, directing the Customer toward payment/next steps instead of proceeding to the monitoring views.

Diverges from Step 8: While viewing the Product Details page, the Customer may select the checkbox labeled 'I want to be notified by email when my bid is exceeded.' The system then sends an automated email alert when the Customer is outbid, enabling passive monitoring instead of requiring the Customer to manually refresh the auction status.

Diverges from Step 8: If overtime bidding is in effect for the displayed item, the system displays the yellow banner 'OVERTIME BIDDING IS ON!' on the Product Details page, indicating that the auction is in an extended-bidding state and that the normal scheduled-close behavior has been altered.
Diverges from Step 11: On the 'My Watch List' page, the Customer can sort the displayed data by clicking column headers, altering the default ending-time sort order while monitoring watched items.

Before main_flow Step 1 (main_flow should be extended to make account-eligibility validation explicit): If the Customer's account has been deactivated (shown in RED in customer records), the Customer cannot use auction monitoring features normally; attempting to access or interact with auction monitoring features requires Supervisor authorization, as indicated by the note '** Deactivating an Account will require a Supervisor's authorization code.' Exit: the use case terminates unless/until a Supervisor supplies an authorization code; monitoring can then be attempted again.

Before main_flow Step 1 (main_flow should be extended to make account-eligibility validation explicit): If the Customer's account is in 'Review Status'—locked because of unresolved auction winnings more than 7 days old (e.g., a PayPal/Amazon Payments order expired after 168 hours and was automatically cancelled)—the system prevents the Customer from bidding on or monitoring active auctions. The Customer cannot self-unlock by paying because the order has already been cancelled and the product returned to inventory. Exit: the use case terminates; a Customer Service Rep must manually remove the Review Status restriction (by updating the account with a credit card) before monitoring can resume.

Before main_flow Step 1 (main_flow should be extended to make account-eligibility validation explicit): If the Customer is subject to the escalation policy—e.g., failed to pay for auction winnings more than three times in a twelve-month period (unless the unpaid count is less than 10% of total winnings) or has an order-cancel rate of 10% or higher—the Customer's bidding access is restricted until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status. This blocks access to auction monitoring functions tied to active bidding. Exit: the use case terminates; monitoring can resume only after CSR intervention restores account functionality.

At sign-in/entry, before main_flow Step 1 (main_flow should be extended to include sign-in/account-status validation): If the Customer's account is closed or suspended, the system prevents sign-in and displays a popup stating: 'We're sorry, this account has been closed [suspended]. If you believe this is an error, please call or email Customer Care at (800) 123-4567 or Auctions@jtv.com.' Exit: the use case terminates; the Customer must resolve the account status with Customer Care before attempting to monitor auctions.

At sign-in/entry, before main_flow Step 1 (main_flow should be extended to include payment-method validation): If the Customer's default payment method is an expired credit card, the system grays out the current page and displays a DIV layer prompting the Customer to enter a new credit card. Exit: selecting 'Yes' takes the Customer to My Account Edit page 3 to update the card, after which the Customer may attempt monitoring again from Step 1; selecting 'No' returns the Customer to the home page and the use case terminates.

Diverges from the product-module entry path described in the trigger (main_flow should be extended to include this navigation step): If the Customer is not signed in and clicks anywhere within a product module (outside the QuickBid button) to view an auction, the system presents the sign-in page. Exit: after completing sign-in, the system delivers the Customer to the Product Details page of the item originally clicked, and the use case resumes at main_flow Step 8.

Diverges from the catalog/search/menu-bar navigation paths by which the Customer enters auction monitoring (these paths are not explicit in main_flow; main_flow should be extended to include them): If the Customer clicks a Menu Bar link that contains no product (which happens routinely for Collectibles), or if a search returns no matching auction items, the system serves a 'No Results Found' page instead of a product/auction listing. The page includes an apology message, a 'Search Tips' section, and a 'May We Suggest' section (with dynamic Omniture-driven suggestions alongside static popular searches). Exit: the Customer refines the search, chooses another category, or returns to the previous page; the use case can be re-entered from Step 1.

Diverges from the path that would display Product Details (main_flow Step 8): If a product does not have an available image, it is ineligible to appear on the Product Details page, search results, or catalog page. Exit: the use case cannot proceed for that item; the Customer must select a different item or return to the previous monitoring view.

Diverges from main_flow Step 14 ('Payment Status' in the 'Items I've Won' section of 'My Bid History'): If the Customer's default payment type is PayPal or Amazon Payments and they have not yet paid for a winning auction, the system displays 'Payment Status' as 'Not Paid' in bold red text, and this status persists until payment is received. The bold-red 'Not Paid' text is a hyperlink to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page. Exit: if the Customer clicks it, the use case hands off to the payment-resolution flow; after payment, the Customer may return to 'My Bid History' and resume monitoring from main_flow Step 13.

After successful monitoring of auction status via the 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History', or 'Recently Ended Auctions' pages, the system maintains and displays real-time dynamic data from the underlying operational database—including a dynamic current date/time, bid-status indicators (e.g., outbid amounts in bold red), payment-status links for unpaid wins, and lists sorted by ending/closing time. The system preserves up-to-date lists for all four monitoring views: My Current Bids, My Watch List, My Bid History (divided into 'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win'), and Recently Ended Auctions.
The 'JTV Current Date/Time' displayed on auction-monitoring pages remains dynamic and updates automatically without requiring the user to refresh the browser.
The system provides vanity URLs www.jtvauctions.com/mybids and www.jtvauctions.com/mywatchlist, allowing the Customer to bookmark direct access to the 'My Current Bids' and 'My Watch List' pages.
On the 'My Current Bids' page, the system displays the items the Customer is currently bidding on, sorted by ending time (soonest on top) by default, with a dynamic JTV Current Date/Time.

On the 'My Current Bids' page, if the Customer's current bid is less than the Current High Bid, the dollar amount in the 'My Current Bid' column appears in bold red text; this outbid indicator persists until the Customer places a new bid or the auction ends.
The 'My Current Bids' page includes active hyperlinks to the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page and the 'Returning Winners Payments' page.

On the 'My Watch List' page, the system displays the items the Customer is interested in but not currently bidding on, sorted by ending time (soonest on top) by default, with a dynamic current date/time and sortable columns.

On the 'My Bid History' page, the system displays the Customer's past bidding activity in two sections—'Items I've Won' and 'Items I Bid On, But Did Not Win'—sorted by ending time with the most recent auctions on top, with dynamic current date/time; the page includes a link to the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page.

In the 'Items I've Won' section of 'My Bid History', the system displays a 'Payment Status' column: unpaid items appear as 'Not Paid' in bold red text that links to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page, and this status persists until payment is received; paid items show 'Paid' when the credit card is the default payment type.
All closed auctions are removed immediately from the site's category pages after closing, and closed auction items do not appear in search results.
Closed auction items remain visible on the 'Recently Ended Auctions' page for exactly 24 hours after closing, after which they are automatically removed from view.

The 'Recently Ended Auctions' page is displayed as a table with columns for Item #, Description, Auction Number, Winning Amount, Winner, and Ending Time, sorted by closing time with the most recent at the top.

When the Customer activates the 'Lowest Bid' button, the system lists all available items sorted by current bid from lowest to highest; when the 'Upcoming Items' button is clicked, the system displays a list/page of scheduled but not yet available items.

On the Product Details page, the system displays real-time auction metrics including 'Current High Bid', 'Opening Bid', 'Bid Increment', 'QuickBid Amount', open/close date/time, and a dynamic 'Time Remaining' countdown that updates without user refresh.

The system maintains and displays an 'Item Bid History' table on the Product Details page, listing up to 25 most recent bids with columns for Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User?, sorted with the most recent bids on top.

If overtime bidding is active, the system displays a yellow banner stating 'OVERTIME BIDDING IS ON!' on the Product Details page, indicating that the auction is in an extended-bidding state and that the normal scheduled-close behavior has been altered.

The system retains and displays the Customer's selection preference for email notification when a bid is exceeded as a checked checkbox on the Product Details page, enabling passive monitoring continuity.

The system preserves and displays the Customer's last five viewed items in a thumbnail row at the bottom of the Product Details page, each linked by SKU, allowing rapid re-access to previously monitored auctions.
The system preserves the Customer's watch list and bid history across sessions, ensuring that watched items and past bids (won or lost) remain accessible upon return to monitoring pages.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Several Product Details postconditions are not anchored in the Main Flow: the overtime-bidding yellow banner ('OVERTIME BIDDING IS ON!'), the persisted email-notification checkbox, and the last-five-viewed-items thumbnail row. Main Flow steps 8-9 display auction metrics and the Item Bid History table, but never state that these additional Product Details page features are displayed. Since the Main Flow does not produce these states, these Postconditions are not reachable from the Main Flow. (slot already rewritten once; further slot_rewrite suppressed)

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Precondition P5 states that closed auctions are removed from category pages immediately after closing OR within the Auctioneer-configured removal interval, but the postcondition claims all closed auctions are removed immediately and do not appear in search results. If a non-zero removal interval is configured, the final monitoring flow cannot guarantee the posted state, so the postcondition is stronger than the upstream precondition allows.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] The Trigger includes entry points from the account area and via global header/footer links such as 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', and 'My Account', but the entry-points precondition enumerates only vanity URLs, Site Map links, canned-search/sidebar links, home category navigation, and Top Auctions product modules. The header/footer and account-area navigation prerequisites are not explicitly covered.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger includes access to account-specific monitoring pages ('My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History'), the account area, account header links, and vanity URLs such as /mybids and /mywatchlist. These paths require the Customer to be authenticated/logged in, but Preconditions never states that an authenticated Customer session exists. The existing 'account not in Review Status' and 'system maintains a watch list/bid history' claims imply an account, but not an active login, so the Trigger cannot start for those paths.

The Trigger enumerates many entry points: direct access to 'My Current Bids', 'My Watch List', 'My Bid History', or 'Recently Ended Auctions'; header links; vanity URLs; Site Map navigation; canned-search/sidebar links; top-level categories; and product modules. Main Flow step 1, however, always begins with 'The Customer navigates to the My Account Page using the My Account link', so it does not pick up the other trigger paths. For example, if the Customer clicks the direct 'My Current Bids' header link or uses /mybids, the flow should continue at 'My Current Bids', not at My Account.

[slot_rewrite] Several Postconditions are not reachable from the Main Flow. The Main Flow's last step is displaying 'Recently Ended Auctions', and the preceding steps only cover My Account -> My Current Bids -> Product Details -> My Watch List -> My Bid History -> Recently Ended. Postconditions, however, additionally assert behaviors absent from those steps: the Product Details overtime-bidding banner, the bid-exceeded email-notification checkbox, the last-five-viewed items row, closed auctions being excluded from search results, and Watch List/Bid History dynamic date/time details. No Main Flow step establishes these states, so the last step does not lead to the full Postconditions state.

The Trigger assumes several concrete entry points exist and are reachable: vanity URLs (www.jtvauctions.com/mybids and /mywatchlist), the Site Map page, canned-search/sidebar links such as 'Closing Soon', 'Hot Items', 'Recently Ended', 'Newly Listed Items', 'Lowest Bid', and 'Upcoming Items', home page top-level categories, and the Today's Top Auctions product module. The Preconditions only say that monitoring pages are implemented, use the global header/footer, have no Endeca navigation, and have no non-functional links. They do not establish that these specific navigation and routing entry points are available, so some Trigger paths are not preconditioned.

The Trigger includes 'Lowest Bid' and 'Upcoming Items' as valid canned-search/sidebar entry points, and the Postconditions explicitly guarantee that Lowest Bid lists all available items sorted by current bid from lowest to highest and that Upcoming Items displays scheduled-but-not-yet-available items. The Main Flow only has a generic response in step 1 saying the system displays the corresponding listing page; it never includes the required behavior for these two entry points. Therefore the Main Flow cannot lead to the Lowest Bid/Upcoming Items postconditions.
